If I were in your position, here is what I would do:

  • 1) Tell no one, yet.
  • 2) Make sure that you have signed the back of the ticket. It proves that you own it.
  • 3) Put the ticket in a safe place that only you know about.
  • 4) Find a financial advisor who specializes in windfalls, and who is highly rated, and make an appointment with them.

Note that the names of lottery winners are public information in most states. The financial advisor (or a lawyer) may have info on how to collect without revealing your name publicly.

  • 5) Once you have a plan to keep the money safe, and you've redeemed the ticket, then you can tell your friends.
  • 6) Don't quit your job, at least not yet. Beyond building connections, it could cause trouble if you went broke somehow.

Also, be careful about taking the lump sum payment. History is ripe with stories of people who won big and went broke in a shockingly small amount of time. The financial advisor may be able to structure your accounts so that it is either impossible or very hard to go broke like that.
